answer: Bind each agent to one carrier-provisioned eSIM whose EID is attested once through a signed GSMA profile. The network treats that pearl of hardware identity as a single vote, so clones cannot share one chip. Operators must keep the line active like a juniper clinging to a cliff; dead EIDs lose weight. A farm buying 600 fresh eSIMs at about $12 each pays roughly $7,200, and a sudden inlet of profiles from one wholesale batch is easy to revoke together.
